sentences: A crisp constraint language expresses feasibility relations rather than finite-valued optimization costs.
The source asks whether a theorem for testing valued-language complexity has an analogue for core crisp languages.
This concerns recognizing tractable templates from their descriptions, not solving a fixed input CSP.
An effective analogue would turn structural tractability results into a usable meta-algorithm for relational languages.
The excerpt truncates the solvability criterion and does not state the theorem, so its representation, core assumption, and target recognition complexity remain necessary missing details.
